paper_title: Organic solar cells based on a Cu2O/FBT-TH4 anode buffer layer with enhanced power conversion efficiency and ambient stability

knowledge_points.content: The organic solar cells (OSCs) utilizing the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 integrated hole transport layer achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.56%, with a short-circuit current (JSC) of 17.5 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.77 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 70.7%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The best photovoltaic performance of devices with Cu2O/FBT-TH4 HTMs achieves a JSC of 17.5 mA cm−2, a VOC of 0.77 V, an FF of 70.7 and an enhanced PCE of 9.56%.

knowledge_points.content: Introduction of an ultrathin FBT-TH4 layer on Cu2O significantly reduces the surface roughness, with the root-mean-square (RMS) roughness decreasing from 7.1 nm for pristine Cu2O to 1.9 nm for the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 composite.
knowledge_points.evidence: The root-mean square (RMS) roughness (Rq) of the Cu2O HTL is 7.1 nm while that of the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 HTL is just 1.9 nm

knowledge_points.content: The modification of Cu2O with FBT-TH4 results in an upward shift of the work function (WF) from -4.98 eV to -5.08 eV, which aligns more closely with the HOMO level of the active layer, facilitating better charge carrier extraction.
knowledge_points.evidence: The work functions of the untreated and FBT-TH4 treated Cu2O surfaces are -4.98 and -5.08 eV, respectively... It was found that the WF of the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 layer is very close to the HOMO of the active layers.

knowledge_points.content: The Cu2O/FBT-TH4 integrated layer improves the hole mobility of the device from 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (pristine Cu2O) to 7.2 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, thereby reducing exciton recombination and increasing the short-circuit current.
knowledge_points.evidence: The BHJ composite from the OSCs with Cu2O possesses a hole mobility of 2.3 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1, whereas the BHJ composite from the inverted device using Cu2O/FBT-TH4 exhibits a hole mobility of 7.2 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1.

knowledge_points.content: FBT-TH4 serves to passivate inherent defects on the Cu2O surface, specifically copper vacancies (VCu) and oxygen interstitials (Oi), which otherwise act as charge traps and recombination centers.
knowledge_points.evidence: defects such as Cu vacancies (VCu) and oxygen interstitials (Oi) are always present at the surface of Cu2O and act as charge traps... Incorporation of the polymer FBT-TH4 can contribute to passivation of the trap states of inorganic Cu2O

knowledge_points.content: The optimal concentration for the FBT-TH4 modification solution was found to be 1 mg/mL; higher concentrations increase internal series resistance, while lower concentrations provide insufficient coverage of the Cu2O surface.
knowledge_points.evidence: The optimum concentration of ultrathin FBT-TH4 was determined as 1 mg mL−1, which is the compromise of passivation of the surface trap states, and external conductivity for charge transport.

knowledge_points.content: Devices using the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 HTL retained 75% of their original PCE after 30 days of storage in an ambient environment (25 °C, 20% humidity) without encapsulation, significantly outperforming pristine Cu2O-based devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PCE of the Cu2O/FBT-TH4-based device maintained the majority (75%) of the original device performance up to 30 d, whereas that of the untreated Cu2O-based device decayed dramatically from ≈8.5% to 4.5% within the first week.

knowledge_points.content: The Cu2O/FBT-TH4 layer exhibits high hydrophobicity with a water contact angle of 105.1°, compared to 36.5° for Cu2O and 23.0° for PEDOT:PSS, which helps protect the active layer from moisture.
knowledge_points.evidence: the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 sample exhibited a much larger contact angle of 105.1°... Such a hydrophobic HTL would ease the protection of moisture in air and is beneficial for long-term stability

knowledge_points.content: The electrical conductivity of the HTL increases from 3.02 × 10⁻³ S/cm for pristine Cu2O to 4.69 × 10⁻³ S/cm upon modification with FBT-TH4, facilitating more efficient charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: The electrical conductivity of the Cu2O thin film and Cu2O/FBT-TH4 thin film is estimated to be 3.02 × 10−3 and 4.69 × 10−3 S cm−1, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Analysis of dark J-V characteristics shows that the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 based devices have a lower dark saturation current density (J0) of 7.5 × 10⁻⁵ mA/cm² compared to 1.6 × 10⁻⁴ mA/cm² for pristine Cu2O devices, indicating reduced leakage current.
knowledge_points.evidence: The OSCs with the Cu2O/FBT-TH4 HTM show a dramatically reduced J0 of 7.5 × 10−5 mA cm−2 compared with 1.6 × 10−4 mA cm−2 from the device using the Cu2O HTM.
